To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of predictive testing in the private sector is a threat to the privacy of the individuals and to the social rights of the individual and the family.

1) Genetic information is a potentially useful tool for selection of applicants for insurance and for job applicants; 2) Genetic information is also a tool for the selection of applicants for social benefits; 3) Genetic information is potentially useful for the selection of job applicants in the private sector and in the public sector;

genetic predictive testing is not an appropriate tool in the context of private life and health insurances, that the access to health insurances should be independent of genetic information, and that the use of genetic data by insurance companies should be limited.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social and ethical issues raised by the development of predictive genetic testing and the possible use of genetic information in the field of insurance.
genetic predictive tests and their implications for the individual.
the following issues: 1. The use of genetic information for insurance purposes and the social implications of genetic information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic information is not a private matter of the individual.
predictive genetic testing should only be performed if the patient is informed about the implications of the test results and if he has given his informed consent.
the use of genetic predictive testing in connection with life insurance and private health insurances should be prohibited.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the European Communities have to develop a legal framework to protect the individual and his/her family against the use of genetic predictive information for selection in insurances and other social attainments.
the European Community should adopt a policy of genetic testing and genetic screening in which the individual has the right to refuse to participate.
we have to be careful not to use genetic testing for selection purposes, and we have to be sure that genetic information is not used in a way that may lead to discrimination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a strong need for the development of new technologies to improve the accuracy, speed, and cost-effectiveness of the genetic testing process.
genetic testing for insurance purposes should be banned.
the genetic information is a potential threat for the individual and his family.
